html:
Jewish girl, born in Frankfurt in 1929, who hid from the Nazis in Amsterdam and kept a diary. She died in a concentration camp in 1945, and her diary became one of the most read books about the Holocaust.

Her family fled Nazi Germany for Amsterdam in 1933 and 1934. The Germans occupied the Netherlands in 1940 and began deporting Jews. In July 1942 the family went into hiding in rooms behind her father's business on the Prinsengracht canal, the "Secret Annex", with four other people.

For two years Anne wrote in her diary about daily life in hiding. In August 1944 they were betrayed and arrested. Anne was sent to Auschwitz and then to Bergen-Belsen, where she died of typhus in early 1945, weeks before the camp was freed. She was fifteen.

Her father, Otto, was the only one of the eight to survive. A helper, Miep Gies, had saved the diary, and he published it in 1947. Their hiding place is now the Anne Frank House museum.
